diffs.message: uses-confirmation-pattern: The confirmation is an inline panel (a Surface with an Alert and an Input) that expands in place on the settings page. It is not a dialog. The diff does not use any dialog or modal component, and the API reference does not list one, so there is no evidence it reached for the design system's confirmation dialog pattern. The inline-warning-style step is the approach the rubric explicitly rules out.

destructive-not-default: Positives: the destructive actions use variant="destructive", which makes them visually distinct. Focus is not on the destructive button: the confirmation input has autoFocus, and the confirm button is disabled until the user types DELETE. Cancel is a secondary button. Negative: the destructive variant is the strongest emphasis in the confirmation panel, so it is arguably the visually primary action. The rubric requires it not to be. Because this is ambiguous, it does not clearly pass.
